headline: Insilico Medicine has chosen ISM1354, a drug designed with AI that blocks a hormone receptor called GIPR, as its next obesity drug candidate.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the announcement was dated 30 Sep 2026, before today's window, and the data are the company's own early animal results.
importance_line: People with obesity or type 2 diabetes could benefit only if the drug later passes human trials, and the results so far are the company's own animal data, while several other GIPR drugs from other developers have run into safety problems in clinical trials.
summary: Insilico Medicine says in its own announcement of 30 Sep 2026 that ISM1354, an AI-designed drug that blocks the GIPR receptor, was well tolerated in a monkey safety study and was absorbed well in four animal species. The drug is still at the preclinical stage, before any human trials, and no outside review of the results is reported.
notes: Original outlet Drug Target Review blocked (HTTP 405); written from Insilico's own announcement, so source and url are the company's. The announcement is dated 30 Sep 2026; Drug Target Review covered it on 2 Oct 2026.
